subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Gongfu Cha: The Art of Skilled Brewing
description: One-minute skill: Gongfu Cha: The Art of Skilled Brewing.

hook.text: Gongfu cha means 'making tea with skill.' It uses tiny pots, lots of leaf, and very short steep times.

buildup.text: A gaiwan or Yixing pot holds just 100–150 ml. Leaves fill a third of the vessel—far more than Western brewing.

discovery.text: Each steep lasts only 10–30 seconds. The same leaves are re-steeped 5–10 times, each infusion revealing new flavors.

twist.text: The first steep is discarded—it 'wakes' the leaves. Flavor begins on the second pour. The best comes around the fourth.

climax.text: Gongfu turns tea drinking into a meditation. Every pour, sniff, and sip is deliberate and unhurried.

punchline.text: Tiny pot, many steeps, infinite layers. Skill unlocks the leaf.

quiz.question: Why is the first steep discarded in gongfu cha?
options: It 'wakes' the leaves—real flavor begins on the second pour

details.summary: Gongfu cha uses a high leaf-to-water ratio and multiple short steepings to extract nuanced, evolving flavors from tea leaves. Each infusion reveals different characteristics. A single serving of oolong or pu-erh can produce eight or more steeps, each one subtly different from the last.
details.whyItMatters: Gongfu cha demonstrates that great tea is an experience that unfolds over time. It maximizes what premium tea leaves have to offer, far beyond a single steep.
takeaways: Gongfu uses high leaf ratios and short, multiple steepings
Each infusion reveals different flavor characteristics
Quality teas can produce eight or more steeps

faq.question: What does gongfu mean in the context of tea?
faq.answer: Gongfu literally means skill achieved through practice. In tea, it refers to the skilled, attentive approach to brewing that extracts the best from each leaf. It is not a fixed ceremony but a method that improves with experience, tea knowledge, and sensitivity.

faq.question: What teas work best with gongfu brewing?
faq.answer: Oolong, pu-erh, and high-quality green and white teas shine with gongfu brewing. Tightly rolled oolongs and compressed pu-erh especially benefit because they unfurl gradually across multiple steeps. Less complex teas like basic black or green may not reward so many infusions.
